items.title: Senate passes major permitting reform bill
items.feedTitle: Senate approves key permitting reform bill, sends to House
items.summary: The Senate approved the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on Thursday with a 62-33 vote, seeking to expedite energy and infrastructure project timelines. The bill represents a significant step toward becoming law, though it still requires House passage. The measure aims to streamline permitting processes across multiple sectors.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin hold historic trilateral summit
items.feedTitle: Inside the historic summit between Trump, Xi and Putin
items.summary: The first-ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia took place Thursday in Shenzhen. The summit resulted in a joint statement with pledges to release more oil and conduct formal talks on nuclear weapons. The meeting signals a potential shift in global power dynamics, though analysts debate its concrete outcomes.

items.title: Coastal storm threatens Thanksgiving travel on East Coast
items.feedTitle: Coastal storm could disrupt Thanksgiving travel along East Coast
items.summary: A significant coastal storm is forecast to impact the northeastern United States this weekend into Monday, bringing heavy rain and gusty winds. The system could disrupt holiday travel for millions heading to Thanksgiving celebrations. Areas from New York to New Jersey are particularly at risk.

items.title: US loses measles elimination status after outbreaks
items.feedTitle: Do you need a measles booster shot now that the U.S. has lost its elimination status?
items.summary: The United States, Mexico, and Bolivia lost their measles-free status this week following stubborn outbreaks that reversed decades of progress. The loss of elimination status reflects growing vaccination gaps across North America. Public health officials are concerned about further spread if vaccination rates do not improve.

items.title: FCC authorizes signal jamming in state prisons
items.feedTitle: FCC votes to allow state prisons to jam signals from contraband cellphones
items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission voted Thursday to allow state prisons to jam cellphone signals smuggled to inmates. Federal authorities consider contraband phones the number-one security threat in US correctional facilities. The move aims to reduce incidents involving inmate-coordinated crimes.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport opens November 30
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: St. Louis MetroLink's new extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport is set to begin service on November 30, marking a major transit milestone for the region. The service extension will improve airport connectivity for residents and visitors. The project represents significant investment in regional transportation infrastructure.

stlouis.title: St. Louis rent increased 3.2 percent last year
stlouis.feedTitle: Report: St. Louis rent increased 3.2% last year
stlouis.summary: A recent report shows St. Louis area rents rose 3.2% over the past year, continuing an upward trend in housing costs. The increase reflects broader regional real estate market pressures. Data suggests affordability concerns for renters across the metro area.

stlouis.title: St. Louis youth face growing housing and stability crisis
stlouis.feedTitle: No bed, no safe place; no stability: The growing crisis facing St. Louis youth
stlouis.summary: A new report highlights a worsening crisis affecting young people in St. Louis, with many lacking safe housing and stable living situations. The issue encompasses homelessness, foster care challenges, and family instability. Local advocates are calling for increased resources and intervention programs.

items.title: UN court rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
items.feedTitle: U.N. Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice issued a historic ruling Thursday finding that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign. The verdict marks the first time a state has been found guilty of genocide by an international court. The ruling sets a precedent for assessing genocidal intent and could have implications for other cases globally.

items.title: Iran escalates attacks on Gulf shipping lanes
items.feedTitle: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain, Further Escalating Fight Over Strait
items.summary: Iran has launched attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, further escalating tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes reflect intensifying regional conflict amid broader Middle East volatility. Officials say the escalation stems from Iranian efforts to pressure Trump into negotiations.

items.title: Russia launches mass missile attack on Ukraine
items.feedTitle: Russia launches mass missile attack against Ukraine after Putin vows retaliation
items.summary: Russia conducted a large-scale missile attack against Ukraine on Thursday following Putin's vow of retaliation for recent strikes. The assault targeted critical infrastructure including bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies. The attack marks continued escalation in the ongoing conflict despite international peace efforts.

items.title: Houthi attack damages Saudi Arabia's tallest tower
items.feedTitle: Houthi Attack Damages Saudi Capital’s Tallest Tower
items.summary: Houthi forces struck Riyadh's tallest building, the PIF tower, in a significant attack on Saudi Arabia's financial hub. Saudi Arabia confirmed the strike and condemned the Houthi attacks. The incident underscores ongoing Yemen conflict dynamics and regional security concerns.

items.title: Europe prepares talks on ending Ukraine war
items.feedTitle: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.summary: European allies of Ukraine gathered in Berlin Thursday for a 'Coalition of the Willing' summit to establish a united negotiating position on peace talks with Russia. European leaders say they are ready for discussions to end the war, though divisions persist on terms. Trump's recent trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi has prompted European concerns about negotiation strategy.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi criticizes India's global geopolitical role
items.feedTitle: "If Congress were in power, India would be sitting at this table": Rahul Gandhi takes dig at BJP after Xi-Putin-Trump trilateral
items.summary: While in the United States, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi argued India is a 'side player' in global geopolitics and criticized PM Modi's handling of international affairs. Gandhi specifically objected to India's exclusion from the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit. His remarks drew sharp responses from BJP leadership.

items.title: Amit Shah declares Kashmir terror threat eliminated
items.feedTitle: Kashmir Free From "India-Born Terrorists" After 35 Years: Amit Shah After Lateef Bhat's Killing
items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that Kashmir is now free from 'India-born terrorists' after 35 years, following the killing of militant Lateef Bhat. The statement marks a significant claim about counter-terrorism progress in the disputed region. Shah emphasized the importance of hunting down fugitives hiding abroad.

items.title: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall on Indian coast
items.feedTitle: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
items.summary: Cyclone Akvan began its landfall process on the Indian coast Thursday, bringing heavy rainfall and squally winds to multiple states. The Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre said the landfall process would extend seven to eight hours. Several districts in West Bengal and Odisha were placed under alert for severe weather.

items.title: Justice Nagarathna: women in office does not ensure equality
items.feedTitle: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
items.summary: Supreme Court Judge B.V. Nagarathna stated that the existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society. The judge emphasized that some women may hold senior positions while others remain excluded from education, employment, and property rights. Her remarks highlight persistent gender inequality despite visible female leaders.

items.title: Dawood Ibrahim aide killed in UP police encounter
items.feedTitle: Dawood Ibrahim's Aide Who Shot Dead Man Near Delhi Minister's Office Killed In UP Encounter
items.summary: Naseem Durrani, a D-Company operative linked to crime boss Dawood Ibrahim and accused in multiple Delhi murders, was killed in a police encounter in Uttar Pradesh. The suspect was allegedly involved in a killing near a Delhi minister's office. The encounter marks continued law enforcement action against organized crime networks.

immigration.title: DOL proposes sweeping PERM labor certification overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The Trump administration's Department of Labor has proposed major changes to the PERM green card certification process, proposed (not final), that would tighten requirements for employers sponsoring foreign workers. The proposal includes ending Schedule A occupational exemptions and strengthening labor market tests. The changes aim to prioritize American workers and have immediate implications for high-skilled immigration pipelines, particularly affecting H-1B to green card pathways.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending USCIS deference on H-1B extensions
immigration.feedTitle: US government is proposing one sentence change in USCIS rules that would change every H-1B visa extension
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed, not finalized, ending the longstanding 'deference' rule that allows USCIS to approve H-1B visa extensions without reviewing prior approvals. The proposal, proposed rule status, would subject approximately 208,000 annual H-1B renewals to stricter scrutiny, potentially increasing Request for Evidence denials. This change could significantly complicate visa renewals for Indian professionals and other foreign workers.

immigration.title: Texas governor-elect pledges to reverse H-1B hiring freeze
immigration.feedTitle: Texas H-1B Freeze: Hinojosa Says She Will Undo Abbott’s Order - immigration-analytics.com
immigration.summary: Incoming Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa announced she will reverse the H-1B visa freeze imposed by her predecessor Greg Abbott on public universities and state agencies. Hinojosa says schools need foreign talent for critical roles. The policy shift signals a potential easing of recent restrictions on skilled foreign worker recruitment in a major state.

items.title: Anthropic closes IPO at $1.3 trillion valuation
items.feedTitle: Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO
items.summary: AI startup Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the NASDAQ Thursday about 17% above its initial public offering price, reaching a $1.3 trillion valuation. The debut marked the largest IPO of all time and created overnight millionaires among thousands of employees. Despite the successful listing, broader US stock markets declined amid concerns over AI valuations and profitability questions.

items.title: Asian stocks plunge as AI sell-off deepens despite Anthropic
items.feedTitle: Asian Stocks Set to Fall as AI Enthusiasm Fades: Markets Wrap
items.summary: Asian stock markets suffered sharp declines Thursday despite Anthropic's record IPO debut, with indexes in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong falling sharply. SoftBank plunged over 16% as AI sector concerns mounted. The sell-off suggests investor caution about AI-related valuations and growth prospects even as new entrants go public.

items.title: Oil prices rise amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.feedTitle: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks in Riyadh fuel supply concerns
items.summary: Oil prices increased Thursday following Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital and financial district. The strikes on critical infrastructure raised supply concerns amid global energy transition discussions. Energy market volatility reflects ongoing Middle East tensions and strategic chokepoint vulnerabilities.

items.title: JPMorgan, Mastercard, Visa data exposed in cyberattack
items.feedTitle: Cyberattack may have exposed Chase Bank and Mastercard customer data
items.summary: A cyberattack exposed customer data at major financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Mastercard, and Visa through a third-party service provider breach. The incident affects millions of cardholders and banking customers across multiple institutions. The breach underscores ongoing cybersecurity vulnerabilities in critical financial infrastructure.

items.title: BILL Holdings to be acquired by TPG for $6 billion
items.feedTitle: BILL Agrees to be Acquired by TPG in Partnership with Corpay
items.summary: TPG and Corpay announced they will acquire finance platform BILL Holdings in a take-private deal valued at approximately $6 billion. The acquisition removes the publicly traded fintech company from the market. The transaction reflects ongoing consolidation in the financial software sector.

cards.title: Anchoring on past approvals
cards.insight: DHS's proposed end to 'deference' on H-1B renewals shows how decision-makers can reverse prior institutional patterns. When new leaders inherit approval systems, they often assume prior decisions were reliable; abandoning that assumption triggers recalculation and delays.
cards.takeaway: Before defaulting to past precedent, ask: who made this rule and under what constraints? Revisiting assumptions can expose hidden costs.

cards.title: Momentum vs. reality check
cards.insight: Anthropic's IPO surged 17% on day one, yet broader markets fell sharply. Investors celebrating the mega-debut ignored signals that AI valuations overall were cracking. Single wins can blind teams to systemic warnings.
cards.takeaway: When one decision succeeds spectacularly, zoom out: are broader conditions actually improving, or just this one actor?

cards.title: Coalition fragility under pressure
cards.insight: Europe's 'Coalition of the Willing' summit aims unified Ukraine negotiation stance, yet Trump's trilateral with Xi and Putin already exposed fissures. Coalitions hold only if members agree on the core threat; when external actors reframe the game, consensus collapses.
cards.takeaway: Before calling alignment 'locked in,' test whether all players define success the same way—and what happens if a third party offers a competing deal.

cards.title: The deference trap
cards.insight: USCIS's 'deference' rule assumes prior officers vetted thoroughly; removing it assumes they didn't. But reversing trust wholesale often causes chaos (backlogs, inconsistency) that harms the very workers it aims to protect.
cards.takeaway: Distrust in a system calls for surgical fixes (audit samples, escalation thresholds) not wholesale reversal. Blunt instruments create collateral damage.

ai.title: US approved 879,000 AI chips for China in six months
ai.feedTitle: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months, House committee says
ai.summary: A House committee revealed Thursday that the Trump administration approved sales of nearly 900,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to Chinese firms over six months. The approvals included sales to companies like Tencent and Alibaba. The disclosure raises questions about export control effectiveness and national security implications of AI chip proliferation.

ai.title: California subpoenas Nvidia over alleged China chip sales
ai.feedTitle: California subpoenas Nvidia as questions about CEO affair, AI chips mount
ai.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued subpoenas to Nvidia regarding reports that the company sold advanced AI chips to China. The investigation follows questions about former CEO Jensen Huang's departure and potential compliance violations. The probe examines whether Nvidia circumvented export restrictions on AI chips.

ai.title: Ex-Anthropic researcher warns of AI concentration risks
ai.feedTitle: 'Insane' to see AI in hands of private giants: ex-Anthropic researcher to AFP
ai.summary: A former Anthropic researcher told AFP it is 'insane' to see advanced AI systems concentrated in the hands of private companies. The criticism highlights ongoing debate about AI governance, safety, and equitable access to powerful systems. The concern reflects broader tensions between innovation speed and responsible development practices.

ai.title: Google's AI outperforms NOAA hurricane forecast model
ai.feedTitle: Google’s AI outperforms NOAA hurricane model in storm-strength study
ai.summary: Google's artificial intelligence system outperformed the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's official hurricane forecast model in a storm-strength prediction study. The finding demonstrates AI's potential for improved weather prediction accuracy. It raises questions about integrating AI forecasting tools into operational meteorology.
